title: Should / Shouldn't
objectives: Use should / shouldn't accurately in A2 contexts.
Understand form, meaning, and typical usage.
Produce short spoken and written examples.
canDo: I can give advice with should and shouldn't.

warmUp.title: Activate prior knowledge
warmUp.prompt: Before this lesson, recall what you know about should / shouldn't. How is it similar or different from Portuguese?
reflectionQuestions: When do native speakers use should / shouldn't?
Can you think of one example?

explanation:
Should + base verb: You should rest. | Shouldn't: You shouldn't drive tired.

Advice, recommendation — not strong obligation.

grammar.title: Should / Shouldn't
grammar.rule: Should + base verb: You should rest. | Shouldn't: You shouldn't drive tired.

reading.title: Should / Shouldn't in Context
reading.text: You look ill — you should go home. You shouldn't drink coffee at night. What should I wear to the interview?

questions.question: What is the main topic of the text?
questions.explanation: The text illustrates this lesson topic.

questions.question: Is this text appropriate for A2 learners?
Which sentence best matches the lesson?

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) using should / shouldn't. Use at least 3 words from the vocabulary list.
rubricHints: Use the target structure at least twice.
writing.modelAnswer: You should see a doctor. You shouldn't skip meals. Take my advice. I recommend this book.

tutorHints: Correct gently and ask the learner to reformulate.
Use English for meta-language when possible at A2.
